title: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine
authors: Guangzhi Xiong, Qiao Jin, Zhiyong Lu, Aidong Zhang
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024, pp. 6233-6251
objective: Systematically benchmark RAG configurations for medical QA
architecture_methods: MedRAG toolkit; 41 combinations of corpora, retrievers and backbone LLMs
models_tools: Six LLMs incl. GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Mixtral (others not verified)
dataset_sample: MIRAGE: 7,663 questions from five medical QA datasets
main_findings: MedRAG improved accuracy of six LLMs by up to 18% over CoT; GPT-3.5 and Mixtral reached GPT-4 level; combining corpora and retrievers performed best; log-linear scaling and lost-in-the-middle effects
limitations: Multiple-choice QA only; no citation-support or faithfulness measurement; dataset/retriever details not verified from abstract
relevance: P3/RQ4: retrieval design drives gains; matched retrieval stack needed for fair baselines
supports_or_contradicts: Supports RAG + combined retrievers; neutral on multi-agent premise
claims_supported: RAG improves medical QA accuracy up to 18% over CoT; combining retrievers is best; position effects exist

title: Almanac: Retrieval-Augmented Language Models for Clinical Medicine
authors: Cyril Zakka, Akash Chaurasia, Rohan Shad, Alex R. Dalal, Jennifer L. Kim, Michael Moor, Kevin Alexander, Euan Ashley, Jack Boyd, Kathleen Boyd, Karen Hirsch, Curt Langlotz, Joanna Nelson, William Hiesinger (author list from arXiv rendering)
venue: NEJM AI (per PMC10857783 / PMID 38343631 search listing); arXiv 2303.01229
published_version_checked: yes (NEJM AI 2024 per PMC listing; published full text not readable, DOI not verified)
metadata_verified_via: ar5iv (arXiv 2303.01229) full text; PMC search listing for venue
objective: Clinical RAG system with citations evaluated vs ChatGPT
architecture_methods: Curated-domain browser + textbook/web database; 1,000-token chunks; HNSW vector store; text-embedding-ada-002; match threshold lambda=0.83 with insufficient-information response; in-text citations
dataset_sample: ClinicalQA: 130 questions (25 x 5 specialties + 5 calculation vignettes) by 5 board-certified physicians
metrics: Physician-rated factuality, completeness, safety (adversarial, omission), preference
main_findings: Factuality +18% absolute on average (cardiology 91% vs 69%, p=0.0189); calculations 5/5 vs 0/5; completeness +4.8% (n.s.); adversarial safety 95% vs 0%; errors of omission 0% for both; physicians preferred ChatGPT 57% of the time; ChatGPT correct sources 56%
limitations: Small author-built dataset; single baseline; preprint numbers may differ from NEJM AI version; omissions; lambda tuning
relevance: P2/P3: abstention-by-threshold design; grounding vs preference mismatch
supports_or_contradicts: Supports grounding for factuality/safety; contradicts assumption that grounded answers are preferred by clinicians
claims_supported: Clinical RAG raises factuality and adversarial safety but not completeness or clinician preference

title: Clinfo.ai: An Open-Source Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model System for Answering Medical Questions using Scientific Literature
authors: Alejandro Lozano, Scott L. Fleming, Chia-Chun Chiang, Nigam Shah
objective: Literature-grounded RAG QA over PubMed/Semantic Scholar
architecture_methods: LLM query generation (3 seeds, union) -> Entrez retrieval -> GPT-3.5 binary relevance filter (+optional BM25) -> per-article summaries -> synthesis + TL;DR with IEEE citations
dataset_sample: PubMedRS-200 (200 QA pairs from systematic reviews; 146 evaluated)
metrics: Retrieval precision/recall; UniEval, COMET, CTC, BERTScore, ROUGE-L, METEOR, chrF, CharacTer; no human evaluation
baselines: GPT-3.5, GPT-4 (no retrieval), Elicit, StatPearls Semantic Search
main_findings: UniEval Overall: GPT-3.5 0.872, GPT-4 0.860, Clinfo TL;DR unrestricted 0.880, Synthesis restricted 0.788; retrieval precision 0.162-0.224, recall 0.052-0.064; source SR retrieved in 96.5% unrestricted cases
limitations: No human evaluation; hallucinated MeSH terms; low retrieval precision/recall; leakage inflates unrestricted results; metric disagreement
relevance: P3/P4: weak retrieval and automated-only evaluation; no-retrieval baseline competitive
supports_or_contradicts: Mixed: no-retrieval baseline beat most RAG variants on one metric
claims_supported: Literature RAG retrieval recall is low; automated metrics disagree

title: Optimization of hepatological clinical guidelines interpretation by large language models: a retrieval augmented generation-based framework
authors: Simone Kresevic, Mauro Giuffrè, Milos Ajcevic, Agostino Accardo, Lory S. Crocè, Dennis L. Shung
objective: Improve GPT-4 Turbo interpretation of EASL HCV guideline via RAG and formatting
architecture_methods: Stepwise ablation: in-context guideline; cleaning + tables to CSV; tables to text lists; prompt engineering; few-shot (54 pairs)
dataset_sample: 20 questions (10 text, 5 table, 5 clinical scenarios), 5 runs each; 2 hepatologist graders
metrics: Expert-graded accuracy; BLEU, ROUGE-LCS, METEOR, custom score; hallucination types
main_findings: Accuracy 43% baseline -> 67% -> 78% -> 90% -> 99% with prompt engineering (p<0.001); few-shot no extra gain; tables 28% baseline; image-table extraction 16%; 124 inaccurate outputs: 90.3% fact-conflicting, 9.7% input-conflicting; similarity metrics did not track accuracy
limitations: One disease/guideline, one model, fixed temperature 0.9, few runs; non-text sources fail
relevance: P1/P3: guideline-grounded RAG; document formatting critical
supports_or_contradicts: Supports guideline RAG with careful formatting; single-agent pipeline reached 99% on small set
claims_supported: Guideline formatting (tables to text) drives large accuracy gains; lexical metrics do not track correctness

title: Detecting emergencies in patient portal messages using large language models and knowledge graph-based retrieval-augmented generation
authors: Siru Liu, Aileen P Wright, Allison B McCoy, Sean S Huang, Bryan Steitz, Adam Wright
metadata_verified_via: PMC (earlier session; reused, not re-opened this session)
objective: Emergency detection in portal messages with KG-RAG
architecture_methods: Prompt-only vs naive RAG vs KG-RAG over nursing triage protocols
main_findings: F1 0.39 prompt-only, 0.59 naive RAG, 0.88 KG-RAG (global search); all differences significant
limitations: Single knowledge source; historical data; n=41 emergencies; correct answers via flawed reasoning possible
relevance: P1/RQ4: retrieval design matters; naive RAG is weak baseline
supports_or_contradicts: Supports structured retrieval; warns against weak baselines
claims_supported: Naive RAG leaves large gaps vs KG-RAG

title: Improving large language model applications in biomedicine with retrieval-augmented generation: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and clinical development guidelines (title unverified on primary page)
authors: Siru Liu, Allison B. McCoy, Adam Wright
metadata_verified_via: Secondary blog; corroborated by citation in ocaf059 (earlier session)
objective: Meta-analyse RAG vs baseline LLM performance in biomedicine
architecture_methods: Systematic review + random-effects meta-analysis
main_findings: Pooled OR 1.35 (95% CI 1.19-1.53), I2=37%, prediction interval 1.01-1.80 (SECONDARY; do not cite until primary checked)
limitations: Outcome definition unknown to us
relevance: P3: modest average RAG gain
supports_or_contradicts: Supports modest, not transformative, RAG gains
claims_supported: RAG gives modest pooled improvement (pending primary check)

title: Retrieval augmented generation for large language models in healthcare: A systematic review
authors: Lameck Mbangula Amugongo, Pietro Mascheroni, Steven Brooks, Stefan Doering, Jan Seidel
objective: Review RAG approaches in healthcare
architecture_methods: PRISMA; Google Scholar + PubMed Jan 2020-Feb 2025
main_findings: 78.9% English / 21.1% Chinese datasets; proprietary GPT models most used; lack of standardised evaluation frameworks; most studies did not assess ethics/safety
limitations: Discussion not read; excludes short conference papers; industry-affiliated authors
relevance: P4: non-standard evaluation of medical RAG
supports_or_contradicts: Supports evaluation-gap claim
claims_supported: Medical RAG evaluation is not standardised

title: An automated framework for assessing how well LLMs cite relevant medical references
authors: Kevin Wu, Eric Wu, Kevin Wei, Angela Zhang, Allison Casasola, Teresa Nguyen, Sith Riantawan, Patricia Shi, Daniel Ho, James Zou
published_version_checked: yes (Nature Communications 2025; preprint arXiv 2402.02008 v1 read in full, differs in design)
objective: Automatically assess whether LLM medical statements are supported by cited sources
architecture_methods: GPT-4 question generation, statement parsing, statement x source verification (supported if any source supports)
models_tools: Published: 7 LLMs incl. GPT-4o with Web Search; v1: GPT-4 (RAG, Bing), GPT-4 API, Claude v2.1, Mistral Medium, Gemini Pro; GPT-4 as verifier
dataset_sample: Published: 800 questions, ~58,000 statement-source pairs; v1: 1,200 questions (MayoClinic, UpToDate, r/AskDocs), >40K pairs, 284 clinician-annotated pairs
metrics: URL validity; statement-level support; response-level support; verifier-doctor agreement
main_findings: Published: 50-90% of responses not fully supported; GPT-4o with Web Search ~30% statements unsupported, ~half responses not fully supported. v1: statement support GPT-4(RAG) 0.694 vs 0.143-0.422 API models; response support 0.543 vs 0.076-0.227; GPT-4(RAG) ~80% MayoClinic vs ~30% r/AskDocs; verifier-doctor agreement 88.0% vs inter-doctor 85.2% (p=0.21); doctors agreed with 95.8% of verifier 'unsupported' labels (110 pairs)
limitations: Measures support not correctness; small validation set; single model snapshot; no kappa; published-version verifier numbers not read
relevance: P3/RQ2: core evidence that citing != supported; LLM verifier accuracy vs clinicians
supports_or_contradicts: Supports need for claim-to-source verification and feasibility of LLM verifier
claims_supported: Even retrieval-enabled LLMs leave ~30% statements unsupported; LLM verifier matches inter-doctor agreement on small set

title: Retrieve-Then-Verify for Evaluating Evidence Support and Hallucination in Large Language Model-Generated Medical Information: Empirical Study
authors: Zhaohui Liang, Cynthia Sheffield, Gisela Butera, Sameer Antani
published_version_checked: yes (accepted 11 Aug 2026, JMIR AI; final version not opened)
objective: Measure evidence support of LLM risk-of-bias assessments
architecture_methods: Claim -> BM25 retrieval from trial report -> verifier verdict (Supported/Contradicted/Not Found/Out of Scope) with quotations
metrics: Evidence support rate; conservative/strict hallucination; accuracy, F1, kappa vs humans
main_findings: Binary accuracy 90-98% but exact 42-71%; evidence support 60-65%; conservative hallucination 34-37%; GPT-5 support 64.3%, strict hallucination 35.7%; BM25 top-1 ~30-31 similar across models
limitations: Single task; lexical retrieval; three OpenAI models; verifier error not reported in abstract
relevance: P3/RQ2: accuracy != grounding; design close to proposed verifier
supports_or_contradicts: Supports claim-level verification
claims_supported: High decision accuracy coexists with 60-65% evidence support

title: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models in Biomedical NLP: Application, Robustness, and Self-Awareness
authors: Mingchen Li, Zaifu Zhan, Han Yang, Yongkang Xiao, Jiatan Huang, Rui Zhang
venue: arXiv 2405.08151 (PMC12637297 record suggests journal publication; venue unconfirmed)
metadata_verified_via: arXiv HTML v2 (earlier session); PMC listing via search
objective: Test robustness and self-awareness of biomedical RAG
architecture_methods: Unlabeled, counterfactual, diverse and negative-awareness testbeds
models_tools: LLaMA2-13B, MedLLaMA-13B, LLaMA3-8B; BM25, Contriever, MedCPT
main_findings: ChemProt F1 86.91 -> 47.79 at 80% counterfactual; no-retrieval beat RAG on MedMCQA; negative-awareness 0.00-1.07%
limitations: Small corpora; single retrieved example; few models
relevance: P3/RQ2: retrieval noise; generators cannot police evidence
supports_or_contradicts: Supports external verifier; contradicts 'RAG always helps'
claims_supported: LLMs rarely recognise unhelpful retrieved content

title: ClashEval: Quantifying the tug-of-war between an LLM's internal prior and external evidence
authors: Kevin Wu, Eric Wu, James Zou
objective: Quantify when LLMs adopt incorrect retrieved content over correct priors
architecture_methods: Perturbed retrieved documents (numeric multiplicative 0.1x-10x, date shifts, categorical); token-probability correction methods
models_tools: GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, Llama-3 Instruct, Claude Opus, Claude Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Flash
dataset_sample: 1,294 questions in 6 domains incl. Drug Dosages (249)
main_findings: GPT-4o adopted incorrect context 60.8% when only prior was correct; context preference falls with deviation size and prior confidence; calibrated correction GPT-4o accuracy 61.5% -> 75.4%, context bias 30.4% -> 10.7%, prior bias 2.1% -> 8.5%; k=5 documents lowered accuracy
limitations: Few domains; fact-based only; over-represents contextual errors; needs token probabilities
relevance: P3/RQ2: wrong retrieved dosages propagate
supports_or_contradicts: Supports checking claims against trusted, versioned sources
claims_supported: LLMs frequently adopt wrong retrieved values incl. drug dosages

title: Contradictions in Context: Challenges for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Healthcare
authors: Saeedeh Javadi, Sara Mirabi, Manan Gangar, Bahadorreza Ofoghi
published_version_checked: no (venue not stated in text; not searched further)
objective: Effect of contradictory retrieved medical documents on RAG answers
architecture_methods: RAG K=5 over PubMed; SPECTER + PubMedBERT-MNLI-MedNLI contradiction detection
dataset_sample: 8,856 queries on 1,476 TGA medicines; 28,873 PubMed docs (1975-2025)
metrics: ROUGE-1; BERT cosine similarity to TGA answers
baselines: Most-similar vs least- vs most-contradicted retrieval
main_findings: Average ROUGE-1 fell 18.2% with contradictory retrieval (Mixtral 0.163 -> 0.131); semantic similarity fell ~8.3%
limitations: Lexical metrics not factuality; sentence-level contradictions; scale/architecture confound
relevance: P3: conflicting sources degrade outputs
supports_or_contradicts: Supports source-quality control
claims_supported: Contradictory retrieved evidence lowers medical RAG answer quality

title: Assessing and Mitigating Medical Knowledge Drift and Conflicts in Large Language Models
authors: Weiyi Wu, Xinwen Xu, Chongyang Gao, Xingjian Diao, Siting Li, Lucas A. Salas, Jiang Gui
objective: Test endorsement of outdated guideline recommendations and mitigation
architecture_methods: Current vs pseudo-outdated recommendation pairs; RAG (k=2) and DPO mitigation
models_tools: GPT-4o, Llama-3-8B, Llama-3.3-70B, Qwen2.5-7B/72B, Gemma-2-27B, Ministral-8B (+Med42, OpenBioLLM in appendix)
metrics: Rejection rate of outdated advice; internal knowledge conflict rate
main_findings: Rejection of outdated advice: Qwen2.5-72B 27.8%, GPT-4o 39.5%, Ministral-8B 80%; larger models not consistently more consistent; RAG+DPO raised alignment 55 -> 81-89
limitations: Synthetic scenarios; two mitigation strategies; DPO only on open models
relevance: P1/P3: outdated guidelines
supports_or_contradicts: Supports current, versioned guideline corpus
claims_supported: LLMs often endorse outdated recommendations; RAG partly mitigates

title: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation
authors: Sewon Min, Kalpesh Krishna, Xinxi Lyu, Mike Lewis, Wen-tau Yih, Pang Wei Koh, Mohit Iyyer, Luke Zettlemoyer, Hannaneh Hajishirzi
objective: Atomic-fact factual precision metric
architecture_methods: Decompose into atomic facts; check support against knowledge source; retrieval + LM estimator
main_findings: ChatGPT 58% (human-judged biographies); automated estimator error <2% (aggregate)
limitations: Biographies/Wikipedia, not medicine
relevance: RQ2: foundation for atomic claim verification
supports_or_contradicts: Supports claim decomposition
claims_supported: Atomic decomposition + retrieval estimates factual precision with <2% aggregate error on biographies

title: MedScore: Generalizable Factuality Evaluation of Open-ended Long-form Medical Answers by Domain-adapted Claim Decomposition and Verification
authors: Heyuan Huang, Alexandra DeLucia, Vijay Murari Tiyyala, Mark Dredze
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2026, pp. 14149-14180
metadata_verified_via: ACL Anthology; arXiv HTML v2 for content
objective: Medical-adapted claim decomposition and verification for factuality
architecture_methods: Condition-aware decomposition (GPT-4o-mini, taxonomy prompt); verification vs internal knowledge, doctor response, or MedCorp (PubMed, StatPearls, textbooks; MedCPT top-10)
metrics: Factuality score; valid-claim rate; human kappa
main_findings: Human eval 382 claims kappa 0.73; valid claims FActScore 17%, MedScore 74.4%, VeriScore 91.7% (24 claims); AskDocsAI FActScore factuality 31.96% (GPT-4o) vs 84.32% (OpenBioLLM) vs 46.10% (Mistral) vs 50.04% (retrieved docs); MedScore 76.54/95.64/78.09/70.07%
limitations: Cannot detect omissions; verifier bias; few doctor-written datasets; small human eval
relevance: RQ2: verifier and corpus choice change unsupported-claim rates
supports_or_contradicts: Supports domain-adapted decomposition; warns scores are verifier-dependent
claims_supported: Factuality scores vary greatly with decomposer, verifier LLM and corpus

title: VeriFact: Verifying Facts in LLM-Generated Clinical Text with Electronic Health Records
authors: Philip Chung et al. (about 30 authors; senior authors Nigam Shah, Nima Aghaeepour)
objective: Verify clinical text against patient EHR with LLM-as-judge
architecture_methods: Sentence or atomic-claim decomposition; EHR fact vector store; BGE-M3 dense/hybrid/reranked retrieval; LLM judge (Supported/Not Supported/Not Addressed)
dataset_sample: VeriFact-BHC: 100 MIMIC-III patients, 13,290 propositions, 25 clinician annotators (3 per proposition)
metrics: Percent agreement with clinician ground truth
main_findings: LLM-written text: VeriFact 92.7% (sentences) / 88.8% (atomic) vs clinician-clinician 84.7% / 88.5%; human-written text clinician agreement 66.6% / 73.3%; top-N=50 retrieved facts best; hybrid/reranked beat dense
limitations: 100 patients, one hospital; poor Not Supported vs Not Addressed distinction; no omission detection; annotators were authors; single LLM
relevance: RQ2: verifier accuracy vs clinicians in clinical text
supports_or_contradicts: Supports feasibility of LLM claim-to-source verifier
claims_supported: LLM judge with retrieval reaches or exceeds inter-clinician agreement on LLM-written text

title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations
authors: Tianyu Gao, Howard Yen, Jiatong Yu, Danqi Chen
objective: Benchmark citation generation and citation quality
architecture_methods: Retrieve evidence, generate answers with citations; automatic fluency/correctness/citation metrics
main_findings: On ELI5 even the best models lack complete citation support 50% of the time; automatic metrics reported to correlate strongly with human judgement (no numbers on abstract page)
limitations: General domain; numbers beyond abstract not extracted
relevance: P3/RQ2: citation support evaluation
supports_or_contradicts: Supports citing != supported
claims_supported: Best models lack full citation support half the time on ELI5

title: RAGAs: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Shahul Es, Jithin James, Luis Espinosa-Anke, Steven Schockaert
published_version_checked: yes (EACL 2024 demo per ACL Anthology listing; content from arXiv 2309.15217)
metadata_verified_via: ACL Anthology search listing; ar5iv full text
objective: Reference-free RAG evaluation metrics
architecture_methods: LLM-based faithfulness (supported statements/all), answer relevance (generated questions, embedding similarity), context relevance (extracted sentences ratio)
dataset_sample: WikiEval: 50 Wikipedia pages, pairwise human labels by 2 annotators
main_findings: Agreement faithfulness 0.95, answer relevance 0.78, context relevance 0.70 vs GPT Score 0.72/0.52/0.63
limitations: Small, author-built, non-medical dataset; single judge model; context relevance hardest
relevance: RQ2: faithfulness metric and its human agreement
supports_or_contradicts: Supports LLM faithfulness checks in general domain only
claims_supported: RAGAS faithfulness agrees with humans 95% on pairwise WikiEval

title: AttributionBench: How Hard is Automatic Attribution Evaluation?
authors: Yifei Li, Xiang Yue, Zeyi Liao, Huan Sun
published_version_checked: yes (Findings ACL 2024 per ACL Anthology listing; numbers from arXiv 2402.15089v1)
metadata_verified_via: ACL Anthology search listing; arXiv HTML v1
objective: Measure difficulty of automatic attribution evaluation
architecture_methods: Binary claim-evidence attributable classification; 7 combined datasets
models_tools: FLAN-T5, AttrScore, T5-XXL-TRUE, FLAN-UL2, Llama-2, RoBERTa-large-mnli, GPT-3.5, GPT-4
dataset_sample: ExpertQA, Stanford-GenSearch, AttributedQA, LFQA, BEGIN, AttrEval-GenSearch, HAGRID
main_findings: Best zero-shot ID 73.6; fine-tuned ID 78.5; fine-tuned OOD 84.2; fine-tuned GPT-3.5 ~80% (77.7); 66.0% of errors fine-grained information insensitivity; ~26.8% human/model evidence access mismatch
limitations: Not medical; label noise
relevance: RQ2: realistic ceiling of automatic attribution accuracy
supports_or_contradicts: Cautions that verifiers miss numeric/name details
claims_supported: Automatic attribution evaluation tops out around 78-84% macro-F1

title: MiniCheck: Efficient Fact-Checking of LLMs on Grounding Documents
authors: Liyan Tang, Philippe Laban, Greg Durrett
objective: Small fact-checkers for grounding documents
architecture_methods: Synthetic GPT-4-generated hard training data; LLM-AggreFact benchmark
main_findings: GPT-4-level accuracy at ~400x lower cost
limitations: Per-dataset numbers and medical coverage not checked
relevance: RQ2/RQ4: cheap verifier option, cost/latency
supports_or_contradicts: Supports small trained verifiers
claims_supported: 770M checker matches GPT-4 on grounding fact-checking

title: Fact or Fiction: Verifying Scientific Claims
authors: David Wadden, Shanchuan Lin, Kyle Lo, Lucy Lu Wang, Madeleine van Zuylen, Arman Cohan, Hannaneh Hajishirzi
objective: Scientific claim verification task and dataset

limitations: Numbers not extracted
relevance: RQ2: biomedical NLI verification foundation
supports_or_contradicts: Supports domain-adapted verifiers
claims_supported: Scientific claim verification benefits from domain adaptation

title: Evidence-based Fact-Checking of Health-related Claims
authors: Mourad Sarrouti, Asma Ben Abacha, Yassine Mrabet, Dina Demner-Fushman
objective: Health claim verification against scientific articles
architecture_methods: COVID-19 claims from search snippets; T5 re-ranking; manual annotation
main_findings: Training on real-world medical claims outperforms synthetic/open-domain claims
limitations: COVID-19 only; numbers not extracted
relevance: RQ2: biomedical NLI verification dataset
supports_or_contradicts: Supports domain-specific verifier training
claims_supported: Health claim verification needs in-domain training data

title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
authors: Jie Huang, Xinyun Chen, Swaroop Mishra, Huaixiu Steven Zheng, Adams Wei Yu, Xinying Song, Denny Zhou
published_version_checked: yes (ICLR 2024 via iclr.cc search listing only)
metadata_verified_via: arXiv abs v2; ar5iv; iclr.cc search listing
objective: Test intrinsic self-correction of reasoning
architecture_methods: Self-correction rounds without external feedback; oracle-label condition; debate vs self-consistency
main_findings: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 -> 38.1 (round 1) -> 41.8; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 -> 89.0; oracle labels GPT-3.5 CSQA 75.8 -> 89.7; GSM8K debate 83.2/83.0 vs self-consistency 85.3/88.2 at 6/9 responses; stronger initial prompt 81.8 -> 75.1 after self-correction
limitations: Reasoning tasks, not medical; ar5iv version not identified
relevance: RQ2/RQ4/P4: critic loops and compute-matched baselines
supports_or_contradicts: Challenges multi-agent/critic premise; supports external verification
claims_supported: Intrinsic self-correction degrades accuracy; debate does not beat matched self-consistency

title: When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs
authors: Ryo Kamoi, Yusen Zhang, Nan Zhang, Jiawei Han, Rui Zhang
objective: Critically survey when self-correction works
architecture_methods: Categorisation of research questions; experimental checklist
main_findings: No prior work demonstrates successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs except in exceptionally suited tasks; works with reliable external feedback; large-scale fine-tuning enables it; many studies overstate benefits
limitations: Survey; abstract only read
relevance: RQ2/RQ4: design of verify-and-revise
supports_or_contradicts: Supports external-feedback verifier; challenges intrinsic critic
claims_supported: Self-correction requires reliable external feedback

title: Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination in Large Language Models
authors: Shehzaad Dhuliawala, Mojtaba Komeili, Jing Xu, Roberta Raileanu, Xian Li, Asli Celikyilmaz, Jason Weston

dataset_sample: Wikidata list questions, closed-book MultiSpanQA, long-form generation
main_findings: Decreases hallucinations across tasks (no numbers on abstract page)
limitations: No external sources; general domain; numbers not extracted
relevance: RQ2: verification loop precedent
supports_or_contradicts: Supports structured verification; not source-grounded
claims_supported: Factored verification questions reduce hallucination

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
authors: Patrick Lewis, Ethan Perez, Aleksandra Piktus, Fabio Petroni, Vladimir Karpukhin, Naman Goyal, Heinrich Küttler, Mike Lewis, Wen-tau Yih, Tim Rocktäschel, Sebastian Riedel, Douwe Kiela

authors: Omid Kohandel Gargari, Gholamreza Habibi
objective: Narrative review of medical RAG challenges

relevance: P1/P3: outdated and heterogeneous guidelines
supports_or_contradicts: Supports corpus-quality concerns
claims_supported: RAG effectiveness depends on source quality, completeness and recency

title: AlignScore: Evaluating Factual Consistency with A Unified Alignment Function
authors: Yuheng Zha, Yichi Yang, Ruichen Li, Zhiting Hu
objective: General factual-consistency (alignment/NLI-style) metric
architecture_methods: Unified alignment function trained on 4.7M examples from 7 tasks (NLI, QA, paraphrase, fact verification, IR, semantic similarity, summarization)
metrics: Factual consistency benchmarks (not named on page)
baselines: Prior metrics incl. ChatGPT- and GPT-4-based metrics
main_findings: Substantially improves on previous metrics; 355M model matches or outperforms ChatGPT/GPT-4-based metrics
limitations: Not medical; per-benchmark numbers not extracted
relevance: RQ2/RQ4: cheap NLI-style verifier option
supports_or_contradicts: Supports small trained verifiers as alternative to LLM judges

title: RAGTruth: A Hallucination Corpus for Developing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
authors: Cheng Niu, Yuanhao Wu, Juno Zhu, Siliang Xu, Kashun Shum, Randy Zhong, Juntong Song, Tong Zhang
venue: ACL 2024 Long Papers (ACL Anthology 2024.acl-long.585, per listing); arXiv 2401.00396v2
published_version_checked: yes (ACL 2024 per ACL Anthology search listing; abstract read on arXiv v2)
metadata_verified_via: arXiv abs v2; ACL Anthology search listing
objective: Word-level hallucination corpus for RAG outputs
architecture_methods: Manual case- and word-level annotation of naturally generated RAG responses with hallucination intensity
models_tools: Diverse LLMs (not listed on abstract page); fine-tuned small LLM detector; prompt-based GPT-4
baselines: Existing detection methods incl. prompt-based GPT-4
main_findings: A relatively small LLM fine-tuned on RAGTruth achieves competitive detection vs prompt-based GPT-4
limitations: Not medical; precision/recall/F1 not extracted
relevance: RQ2: RAG hallucination detection benchmark and verifier training data
supports_or_contradicts: Supports trained detectors; shows RAG outputs still hallucinate
claims_supported: Fine-tuned small detectors can rival GPT-4 prompting for RAG hallucination detection
